identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log – Forklift FL-2 (Toyota 8FGU25, propane), September 2026 – Portland Warehouse

scan.summary: This is your own daily pre-shift inspection log for one propane forklift (unit FL-2) at the Portland warehouse for September 2026. Operators fill in a row each day to show they checked the truck before driving it. A log like this is judged on whether it is complete and up to date. This one has missing days, stops on September 18, and records a horn defect with nothing showing it was fixed. The supervisor review line is also blank.
scan.freshness_note: The last entry is Friday, September 18, 2026, nine days before today (2026-09-27). The weekdays September 21–25 have no entries in this file. Ask the warehouse whether there is a continuation sheet for FL-2 covering Sep 21 onward. If there is none, find out whether the truck ran that week.

gaps.title: No entries after Sep 18
gaps.description: The log stops on Friday, September 18. It has no entries for the working days September 21–25, 2026, and nothing on the page says the truck was out of service. Either a second sheet exists or the checks were not recorded.
gaps.fix: Find and file the continuation sheet for Sep 21 onward. If the truck ran with no inspection recorded, write down why, and restart daily pre-shift checks before each shift. Look at the hour meter to confirm whether the truck was used on those days.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), adopted in Oregon by OAR 437-002-0220

gaps.title: No inspections on Sep 3 and Sep 4 while the truck was running
gaps.description: There are no entries for Thursday Sep 3 or Friday Sep 4. The hour meter goes from 4,819 on Sep 2 to 4,834 on Sep 7, a rise of 15 hours. That is more than one normal day of use (about 6–7 hours), so the truck appears to have run on at least one day with no pre-shift inspection recorded.
gaps.fix: Ask the operators whether the truck was used on Sep 3 or Sep 4. Do not fill in entries after the fact. Instead, add a dated note saying what happened, and remind operators that a check is required before every shift the truck is used.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), adopted in Oregon by OAR 437-002-0220
gaps.locator: Page 1, between the Sep 2 and Sep 7 rows
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Horn defect with no record of removal from service or repair
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn was marked as a defect ('Horn not working'). The next day it was ticked OK, but nothing shows who repaired it or whether the truck was taken out of service. The hour meter rose about 6 hours between the Sep 9 and Sep 10 readings. That suggests (inferred) the truck was driven on Sep 9 with the horn not working.
gaps.fix: Find the repair record or work order for the horn and file it with this log. If there is none, write down what was done and who did it. Set a rule that a truck with a safety defect is tagged out until it is repaired, with the repair noted on the log.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(1) and (q)(7), adopted in Oregon by OAR 437-002-0220

gaps.title: Supervisor review not signed
gaps.description: The supervisor review signature and date lines at the bottom of the log are blank. No specific rule requires a supervisor signature. This is a control on your own form, and the blank line means nobody caught the missing days or the open horn defect.
gaps.fix: Have the warehouse supervisor review the log, sign and date it, and add notes on the gaps above.
gaps.citation: No specific rule requires a supervisor signature. This is your own form's control.

scan.confidence_notes: The file read cleanly. Both pages are legible and the text matches the table images. Where each item came from: the company name, site, truck and month are in the page 1 header. The last entry date (Sep 18) and the operator key are on page 2. Weekdays for September 2026 were worked out from the calendar (Sep 3–4 are Thursday and Friday, Sep 21–25 is a full work week), so those are inferred. The claim that the truck was driven on Sep 9 with the horn not working is also inferred, from the hour meter. I confirmed that Oregon adopts 29 CFR 1910.178 by reference in OAR 437-002-0220. Oregon also has additional state rules for powered industrial trucks, and I did not check this log against those. The sentence on page 2 about the hour meter reads like a note someone added later rather than part of the original form. I treated it as document text but relied on the hour readings themselves. The gaps found this time are the same four still open from the earlier reading, and no new ones were found. This is a record, not a program, so it was judged only on whether it is complete and recent.
